summary.headline: Inox Wind Q2 FY27 revenue rose 58% QoQ to Rs 1,378 crore, but management dropped FY27 growth guidance and kept the ~20% margin goal for the long term.
summary.overview: Inox Wind's consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue was Rs 1,378 crore, up 58% QoQ, with adjusted EBITDA flat QoQ at Rs 238 crore and EBITDA margin depressed by commodity and raw material inflation. Management said the shift to equipment supply (targeted at ~75% of third-party order book) has cost near-term growth and order inflow, and it withdrew the earlier FY27 growth and margin guidance. Inox Green reported Q2 total income of Rs 113 crore (+12% QoQ) and PAT of Rs 44 crore (+8% QoQ), excluding Windworld income, as its ~4.5 GW Windworld O&M acquisition was paid for and will be consolidated from Q3 FY27. Management highlighted that Windworld income was not in the P&L this quarter, which is why reported margins looked low.

financial_highlights.value: approximately 3.8 GW as of October 2026 (over 24 months visibility)
approximately 12.5 GW (10.4 GW wind, 2.1 GW solar) as of September 2026

segments.name: Inox Wind (equipment and EPC)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 1,378 crore (+58% QoQ) with flat adjusted EBITDA of Rs 238 crore; margin hit by commodity inflation. Equipment supply was about 61% of third-party order book as of 26 October, with a target of ~75%.

segments.name: Inox Green (O&M / OEDM)
segments.commentary: Q2 total income Rs 113 crore and PAT Rs 44 crore, excluding any Windworld income. Windworld (~Rs 580 crore FY26 revenue) to be consolidated line by line from Q3 FY27, with Windworld OEDM margin targeted above 45%.

guidance_outlook: Inox Wind: no FY27 revenue guidance; management said FY27 will not reach the previously guided ~75% growth and 20-22% margin.
Inox Wind: FY28 revenue target of approximately Rs 7,500 crore, to be reviewed at end of Q4 FY27.
Inox Wind long-term EBITDA margin objective ~20%, to be judged on an annual basis; Q2 margin would have been above 20% with Windworld income included.

Inox Wind expects Windworld consolidation from Q3 FY27, which management estimates could roughly double Q3 revenue versus Q2 Rs 113 crore for Inox Green (~Rs 120-150 crore Windworld revenue quoted in Q&A).
Inox Wind expects working capital days to fall below 150 by end of FY28; H2 typically ~70% of annual revenue.
Inox Green: other investment (~2 GW wind OEDM) expected consolidated by Q4 FY27 subject to approvals; significant operating cash flow expected from next year as cash tax deferred.
capex_capacity: Next-generation 4X wind turbine platform: prototype installed, commissioning expected shortly, commercial launch targeted by end FY27.
Rohtak facility in Gujarat fully geared to produce blades for the 4X platform.

Expanding transformer capacity for 4X series; plans for medium transformers (8-20 MVA) and larger transformers, plus inverters, unit substations and electronic control systems. Investments are calibrated with short payback.
Inox Green: Windworld O&M acquisition payment completed after Rs 300 crore QIP in October 2026 and NCLT-approved transfer; other investment awaiting regulatory approvals.
demand_pricing: Inox Wind repeat orders in Q2 from NLC India, Terra Clean Energy, a Hero Future Energies subsidiary (rendered as 'a holy word subsidiary' in transcript) and an IPP; pipeline of ~5 GW of potential tenders from NTPC, IOC and SECI over 4-5 months.
India added 3.2 GW of wind in H1 FY27 versus 6.05 GW in all of FY26; MNRE expects 7.5-8 GW wind additions in FY27.
Power demand grew 15% YoY in Q2; 5.8 GW of renewable tenders in Q2, of which 2.1 GW standalone wind.
Management sees no meaningful domestic pricing pressure despite possible entry of Adani Wind into third-party market; said pass-through clauses apply in many contracts.

qa_highlights.question: Does Inox Green have an order or capacity target for FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: No specific target; order book of nearly 4 GW equals about Rs 20,000 crore revenue over two years and gives visibility for 2.5-3 years. Focus is on free cash flow and balance sheet.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 growth of 75% and 20-22% margin guidance be met?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will not reach those numbers because of the strategy change; some orders were given up and some FY27 revenue let go, though FY28 guidance is conservative.

qa_highlights.question: Will Windworld add about Rs 150 crore to Q3 revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is broadly in line, around Rs 120-150 crore, with the Windworld agreement signed mid-October, so Q3 revenue could roughly double from Rs 113 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why has Inox Green's wind AUM stayed at 3.94 GW despite new additions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said standalone wind O&M additions were made this quarter, with a lag between turbine supply and commissioning. Solar capacity is being exited because it is low margin, with only hybrid solar retained.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Windworld margin path and how much is other income?
qa_highlights.answer: Windworld margin currently about 25-30%, with potential to reach about 40% after value-added services and cost cuts; about Rs 10 crore of the Rs 24 crore other income is treasury income. Inox Green will own 75% of Windworld with minority interest.

qa_highlights.question: Is there pricing pressure domestically?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no pricing pressure is seen yet; limited competition and strong demand, with wind gaining value in peak hours as solar tariffs weaken without storage.

risks_watch: Inox Wind margin pressure from commodity and raw material inflation linked to the Middle East conflict, with management saying the impact is temporary.
Working capital: H1 receivables elevated and inventory built ahead of H2; management expects inventory to moderate but gave no timing.
Inox Wind CEO Sanjeev Agarwal resigned (advisor until end-December); Sai Babu Vattikuti joined as MD of wind business.
Windworld integration: margin uplift depends on salary rationalization, value-added services and repricing; consolidation timing depends on approvals.
Demerger of power evacuation infrastructure business to a separately listed entity: information memorandum filed; listing expected in next 1-2 quarters, subject to approvals.
Inox Green's standalone O&M growth depends on the lag between turbine supply and commissioning.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term prospects and balance sheet, but openly defensive on FY27: management repeatedly declined to give FY27 numbers, withdrew prior growth and margin guidance, and framed the shortfall as a deliberate strategy trade-off. Answers on the Inox Green AUM and the Windworld timeline were more evasive and led to follow-up questions.

we would refrain from providing specific revenue guidance for FY 27 at this stage.
there is no point having a top line of 100 crores and making 5 crore margin.
we are virtually in debt free currently there is a miniscule debt

Rohtak facility (Gujarat) geared to produce blades for 4X platform

growth.why: Management withdrew FY27 growth and margin guidance (the ~75% growth and 20-22% margin targets will not be reached) and set only an FY28 revenue target of ~Rs 7,500 crore, reviewed at end Q4 FY27; backing is partial, with 4X platform launch, transformer/blade capacity and Windworld consolidation from Q3 FY27, against a 3.8 GW order book after discontinued orders.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA flat QoQ at Rs 238 crore on commodity inflation; management withdrew FY27 20-22% margin guidance but holds ~20% long-term objective, and Windworld margin (25-30% now, potential ~40%) lifts Inox Green mix from Q3 FY27.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Windworld ~4.5 GW O&M consolidated line by line from Q3 FY27 (acquired, not built) and 4X platform commercial launch targeted end FY27; wind turbine availability already at 96.2% with equipment supply rising to ~75% target.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Windworld consolidation could roughly double Inox Green Q3 revenue from Rs 113 crore (Rs 120-150 crore Windworld quoted), and India added 3.2 GW wind in H1 FY27 with MNRE expecting 7.5-8 GW in FY27; but Inox Wind FY27 growth will not reach ~75%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Transformer capacity expansion for 4X and planned medium transformers (8-20 MVA) are being calibrated for short payback, and ~96.2% utilisation is high, but no new capex amount was disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 growth (~75%) and 20-22% margin guidance were withdrawn, with management saying FY27 will not reach them after a deliberate shift to equipment supply that cut order inflow.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY28 revenue target of ~Rs 7,500 crore is to be reviewed at end Q4 FY27, and commodity inflation is pressuring margins at Rs 238 crore flat EBITDA, though management calls the impact temporary.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Next-generation 4X wind turbine platform prototype installed with commercial launch targeted by end FY27; blades produced at Rohtak for the 4X platform.

rows.label: Order book 3.8 GW, ~24 months visibility
rows.why: Order book fell to ~3.8 GW from discontinued orders, though H1 FY27 inflow was ~1.85 GW and ~5 GW of tenders from NTPC, IOC and SECI are in pipeline over 4-5 months.

rows.label: Demerger of power evacuation infrastructure business
rows.why: Information memorandum filed with listing expected in next 1-2 quarters, subject to approvals.

rows.label: Inox Green ~2 GW wind OEDM consolidation
rows.why: Other investment (~2 GW wind OEDM) expected to be consolidated by Q4 FY27 subject to regulatory approvals, which are still pending.

tone.note: Management was confident on long-term margins, balance sheet and the Windworld consolidation, but defensive on FY27 after withdrawing guidance; analysts pressed on Inox Green AUM stalling at 3.94 GW and on the Windworld timeline and margin path.
